Let other agents ride your dragon

Source: vignettes/articles/other-agents.Rmd
other-agents.Rmd

Your dragon already knows your documents. Now Claude, or any chat you run from R, can ask it directly: search a document set, answer from it with citations, read new documents in, list your sets and runs, check on a training run.

From an ellmer chat 

library(dragonfarm)
chat <- ellmer::chat_anthropic()
chat$register_tools(dragon_ellmer_tools())
chat$chat("What do my FDA guidances say about covariate adjustment?")

The chat decides when to search, reads the excerpts it gets back, and answers with their sources.

From Claude Desktop, Claude Code, or any MCP client

Add a server to the client’s configuration:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "dragonfarm": {
      "command": "Rscript",
      "args": ["-e", "dragonfarm::dragon_mcp_server()"]
    }
  }
}

Six tools appear in the client: search_documents, answer_question, read_documents, list_document_sets, list_runs, and run_status. Searching and listing are marked read-only, so clients can tell them apart from read_documents, which writes a document set.

What keeps it tame

  • Every call is checked first. Arguments must fit the tool’s contract, so a bad call comes back as a plain code (NOT_A_SET, INVALID_ARGUMENTS) instead of a crash.
  • Agents follow a policy. Name the caller as an agent, dragon_ellmer_tools(agent = "answer"), and it may only use that agent’s tools. The policy also says which kinds of call wait for a person: training, promoting a model, deleting anything, and anything that leaves your machine.
  • Every call is written down. Each one, refused ones included, lands in a small catalogue in your runs folder, in an append-only log.
  • Your documents stay home. The tools run on your machine; only what the chat model itself sees, the question and the excerpts it gets back, goes to the model you chose to chat with.
